reading.title: Bioluminescence in Deep-Sea Organisms
reading.passage:
Bioluminescence, the production of light by living organisms, represents one of the most fascinating adaptations in marine biology. Approximately 90% of deep-sea creatures possess the ability to generate light through chemical reactions involving luciferin and luciferase enzymes. This phenomenon serves multiple critical functions in the abyssal environment where sunlight cannot penetrate. Many species utilize bioluminescence for predation, emitting lures that attract unsuspecting prey in the perpetual darkness. Others employ it as a defense mechanism, producing sudden flashes that confuse potential predators or serve as warning signals to indicate toxicity.

The ecological significance of bioluminescence extends beyond individual survival. Recent research indicates that bioluminescent organisms play a crucial role in deep-sea food webs, with their light production influencing predator-prey dynamics at depths exceeding 1,000 meters. Scientists have documented over 1,500 species capable of producing light, ranging from dinoflagellates to anglerfish. Furthermore, the study of bioluminescent proteins has revolutionized biomedical research, enabling scientists to develop innovative diagnostic tools and track cellular processes in unprecedented detail. This convergence of marine ecology and biotechnology demonstrates how understanding natural phenomena can yield substantial practical applications.

questions.q: According to the passage, what percentage of deep-sea creatures can produce bioluminescence?
options: Approximately 50%
Approximately 75%
Approximately 90%
Approximately 100%
questions.explanation: 첫 번째 문단에서 'Approximately 90% of deep-sea creatures possess the ability to generate light'라고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.q: What can be inferred from the passage about the deep-sea environment?
options: It contains high levels of sunlight
It is characterized by complete darkness
It supports only bioluminescent organisms
It experiences regular seasonal changes
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'in the abyssal environment where sunlight cannot penetrate'라고 언급되므로, 심해는 태양광이 닿지 않는 완전한 어둠의 환경임을 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.q: The word 'emitting' in the first paragraph is closest in meaning to
options: absorbing
producing and sending out
controlling
storing
questions.explanation: 'emitting'은 '방출하다', '내보내다'라는 의미로, 여기서는 생물이 불빛을 '생성하여 방출한다'는 뜻입니다. 'producing and sending out'이 가장 정확한 의미 입니다.

questions.q: Why does the author mention bioluminescent proteins in the final sentence?
options: To explain how bioluminescence evolved
To demonstrate the practical applications of studying natural phenomena
To criticize current biomedical research methods
To compare different types of marine organisms
questions.explanation: 저자는 생물 발광 단백질 연구가 의료 진단 도구 개발로 이어졌음을 언급하여, 자연 현상 연구가 실제적 응용으로 이어질 수 있음을 보여주기 위함입니다.

paraphrasing.original: Bioluminescence, the production of light by living organisms, represents one of the most fascinating adaptations in marine biology.
paraphrasing.paraphrase: The ability of living creatures to generate illumination through chemical processes, known as bioluminescence, exemplifies remarkable evolutionary development in oceanic life.
paraphrasing.tip: 명사구를 재구성하고 동의어(production→generate, fascinating adaptation→remarkable evolutionary development)로 치환하여 의미를 유지하면서 표현을 다양화

paraphrasing.original: Many species utilize bioluminescence for predation, emitting lures that attract unsuspecting prey in the perpetual darkness.
paraphrasing.paraphrase: To capture food in the endless darkness of the deep sea, numerous organisms emit light-based traps designed to lure unaware victims.
paraphrasing.tip: 능동형 구조를 '~하기 위해'의 목적절 형태로 변환하고, 'emitting lures'를 'emit light-based traps'로 구체화하여 표현

paraphrasing.original: Scientists have documented over 1,500 species capable of producing light, ranging from dinoflagellates to anglerfish.
paraphrasing.paraphrase: Research has identified more than 1,500 light-producing organisms, spanning a diverse range from microscopic dinoflagellates to large anglerfish.
paraphrasing.tip: 주어를 'Scientists'에서 'Research'로 변경(능동→준수동)하고, 'ranging from'을 'spanning a diverse range from'으로 확장하여 표현 강화

speaking.prompt: Some people are morning types who are most productive early in the day. Others are evening types who prefer working late into the night. Which do you prefer and why? Include specific reasons and details.
model_sentences: I definitely prefer being a morning person because I find that I can accomplish more before noon.
First of all, when I wake up early, my mind is fresh and I can focus on difficult tasks without distractions.
For example, last semester I started studying for exams at 6 AM instead of late at night, and I actually retained the information much better.
Additionally, morning productivity allows me to enjoy my evenings for relaxation and social activities instead of feeling exhausted.
In conclusion, I believe the morning schedule is more beneficial for both my academic performance and my overall well-being.

listening.title: Photosynthesis in Marine Algae
listening.script: Professor: Today we're examining photosynthesis in marine algae, which differs significantly from terrestrial plants. Student: What makes it different, Professor? Professor: Well, deep-sea algae receive limited sunlight, so they've evolved specialized pigments like chlorophyll-b and xanthophyll. These additional pigments capture wavelengths that standard chlorophyll cannot access. Student: So they're more efficient? Professor: Precisely. They maximize light absorption despite limited availability. Additionally, the osmotic pressure in saltwater environments requires algae to develop thicker cell walls and unique photosynthetic pathways. Some species even practice cyclic photophosphorylation at night, storing energy in ATP molecules. This remarkable adaptation allows them to photosynthesize continuously, even during darkness. The implications for understanding plant biochemistry and developing sustainable biofuel sources are enormous. Any questions? Student: Could we replicate this in laboratories? Professor: That's an excellent question we'll explore in next week's lab session.

They capture light wavelengths that standard chlorophyll cannot access
They reduce the algae's need for saltwater
They increase photosynthesis only during the day

questions.q: Why does the professor mention cyclic photophosphorylation?
options: To explain why deep-sea algae have thicker cell walls
To demonstrate how deep-sea algae can continue photosynthesizing even in darkness
To describe the osmotic pressure in saltwater
To show why terrestrial plants are more efficient
questions.explanation: 교수는 '밤 동안에도 ATP에 에너지를 저장하는 방식으로, 이를 통해 연속적인 광합성이 가능하다'고 설명하여 암흑에서도 광합성이 가능한 메커니즘을 보여줍니다.
